title: Arizona's 7th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Arizona's 7th Congressional District pits freshman Democratic incumbent Adelita Grijalva against Republican challenger Daniel Francis Butierez Sr. The district, which covers a large swath of southern Arizona including Tucson, Yuma, Nogales, and parts of the Phoenix suburbs, is a safely Democratic seat (D+13) that has been held by the Grijalva family for over two decades. Grijalva won a September 2025 special election to succeed her late father, Rep. Raúl Grijalva, and is now seeking a full two-year term. The contest highlights contrasting views on border security, economic development, and the role of the federal government in a district that spans nearly 300 miles of the U.S.-Mexico border.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The primary election is scheduled for July 21, 2026, and general election polling has not yet been released.

candidates.name: Adelita Grijalva
candidates.summary: Adelita Grijalva is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 7th Congressional District, first elected in a September 2025 special election to succeed her late father, Rep. Raúl Grijalva. She previously served on the Pima County Board of Supervisors and the Tucson Unified School District Governing Board, and spent 25 years as director of the Pima County Teen Court juvenile diversion program. Her campaign emphasizes education access, economic opportunity, environmental policy, and protecting working families.

career_history.description: Youngest woman ever elected to the board; served 18 years.

candidates.name: Daniel Francis Butierez Sr.
candidates.summary: Daniel Francis Butierez Sr. is a small business owner and the Republican candidate for Arizona's 7th Congressional District. He owns Butierez/Express Painting and is a third-generation Arizonan whose campaign focuses on border security, tax cuts for small businesses, and responsible mining for economic development. Butierez was wrongfully convicted of a crime in the 1990s, spent time in prison, and was later exonerated by the state; he describes his life experiences as shaping his views on criminal justice reform and second chances.
